en: Are no enemy a warrior can bring low!
Blazing anew as they are depleted,
Growing stronger again from their roots,
The Kytay are an inexhaustible people.
No man has conquered them;
That is why the Kytay
Are called the Kytay of Kakanchyn!
No man has overcome them in combat;
Against that accursed Kakan,
None who fought has survived.
With Beejin bathed in radiance,
My son Manas, listen:
Let us leave unharmed, without fighting.
By attacking an inexhaustible people,
Alas, my boy, hear my words,
What inheritance shall we gain?
Against the people of Kakanchyn,
Why should we contend?
Can a mortal defeat them in combat?
On this dark day, my son, let us leave!
Those unbelievers, as countless as a cow's hairs,
Swarming like ants—
Such are Kakanchyn's people.
They let no attacker escape;
Drinking his blood is their custom.
When their ruler gave the order,
To seize and bind you,
Their mighty champions came!
If we stand on opposing sides,
Firing guns and drawing bows,
And fight amid the crashing shots,
With arrows whistling,
With all they strike splintering,
With blood pouring in streams,
If we perish, struck by shot,
This will be no splendid deed.
Against Beejin, which no one dares touch,
We are no match.
Know that my counsel is sound;
You were a rash-hearted boy,
My lion Manas, heed me!
When we wage a tumultuous battle,
Thrusting spears and drawing bows,
When we stand shouting our cries,
If we fight harder day after day,
With warriors dying, unheeded by beasts,
If we stand shouting in battle,
To keep ascending the heights,
I have no land like Ala-Too here.
If we clash with shouts,
If we are being exhausted,
Our feet slipping from the stirrups,
Our rumps sliding from the saddles,
Those who would fight fiercely,
When our strength begins to fail,
Those who would rescue us,
Wearing black sable caps,
Fearless wolves of war—
Your solitude is beyond measure;
Those who would all become our companions,
The Kyrgyz people are not here!
Know that this is my counsel:
You were the support of forty hearths,
You were the one at their forefront.
If you heed me, Khan Manas,
On this side of Altay,
At the edge of Sary-Talaa,
Where no raven croaks,
Where no crow flies cawing,
Where there is no grass to nibble,
Where there is no water to sip,
Let us bar their way there for six days;
Let us wage a fierce struggle!
Firing guns and drawing bows,
Holding the narrow passage,
Fighting there for many days,
Once the sorrowing people have gone beyond,
Once the forty humiliated households
Have passed to the farther side,
Until these people escape,
To Kichi-Zhyldyz and Chong-Zhyldyz,
Until the forty households reach there,
Until the people escape,
Let us fight like dogs.
My boy Manas, heed me.
Let us preserve the lives entrusted to us!
Once we have passed Zhyldyz,
Its plains are forest, its mountains snow;
There stand the heights of Ala-Too,
The land that bore your seven forefathers,
The land where your mother tied the birth cord,
The land that became our blessing.
That is the ridge where we can settle securely.
When we reach a land to lean upon,
We shall not weary of battle;
There, remaining as our inheritance,
Are the scattered and destitute people!”
When Akbaltay had said this,
His roar split stones,
His shout split heads;
White teeth like a gate,
Teeth unlike those of other people,
Now flashed into view.
The leopard never sated with blood
Now unleashed his full wrath.
Manas began the tumult;
When your gray-maned hero surged,
The mountain shook:
“Until I reached twelve,
Wandering, exiled and humiliated,
I passed my days in Altay.
I have grown to manhood, become a warrior,
Become the equal of heroes' sons.
Now, Baltay, I will not heed you!
Grappling and fighting,
Spear in hand, I will break their ranks.
If God takes it, here is my life;
If death has come, I will fall to shot!
I will die rather than live thus.
If, instead of dying here,
I flee shamelessly, stumbling away,
To those who hear and see,
To those who know and learn of it,
'Manas fled from the Kytay,' they will say;
'That accursed Burut
Scattered all his possessions,' they will say.
If all the peoples gossip thus,
How shall I answer?!
If I should happen to flee,
These Kyrgyz, these forty households,
If the Kytay overtake them from behind
And they should all be slaughtered,
Will not everyone know my dog-like baseness?
Tomorrow, on the Day of Judgment,
Those dear people who died,
Will they not ride me as a black donkey?
Trailing endless curses,
What inheritance would I gain?
For this people, these forty households,
Let me sacrifice myself!
Alas, Baltay, what are you saying?!
I thought I knew much of you;
Among the forty households, elder Baltay,
I had always called you wise!
Since coming to this Altay,
To the black Kalmyks and Manchus
Paying tribute every year,
Caught in the cold blizzard,
You have been ruined.
Your schemes have run out;
Oh, my elder, Khan Baltay,
You have become good for nothing!
While I am still alive,
How can I yield my companion to the Kytay?
With the Manchus who attacked us,
Let me try exchanging severed heads!
Alas, Baltay, what are you saying?
If we wage a dog's battle,
Will they not say, 'Manas fled'?
Relentlessly tracking our every step,
The Kytay will pursue relentlessly;
Will they not devour us that way?
Will they not know your fear?
If those faithless ones pursue you,
Will they not drive you as far as Mecca?
Will they not overtake you on every side?
Will they not scatter your countless livestock?
'The bloodstained Burut fled,' they will say;
Will they not mount their rhinoceroses,
Will they not sound their trumpets,
Will they not plunder your goods,
Will the Kytay not wreak havoc?
Alas, Baltay, what are you saying?
Accursed Baltay, what are you saying?
Let dogs hear these words of yours,
Let mountains with high passes hear,
Let fiercely flowing waters hear,
Let the dark grave dug open hear;
Who else should hear them?
What Allah has inscribed,
How can I leave without seeing it?
Without showing my boundless valor,
Without letting my people travel freely,
From those mother-cursed unbelievers,
How can I flee in panic?
If mighty Allah supports me,
Let me keep grappling with them!
While my precious head remains,
How can I fear a governor?
While my head has Khizir's blessing,
How can I flee the Kytay?
Esenkan has grown eager;
Let us slaughter one another!
Will not some governor spur his mount
And bring his khan the news?
'You praised him falsely;
He has fled,' will he not say?
'Over the pass of Tolgonush Mountain
He has gone,' will he not say?
'His abundant, countless livestock
He scattered and left,' will he not say?
'Unable to wheel and thrust his spear,
That huge, mountain-like Burut
Panicked and left,' will he not say?
If the rumor reaches Beejin,
Among Kakanchyn's people,
Will the Kytay's day not dawn?
Swarming forth, will these swine
Not pursue us as far as Mecca?
Will they not chant their taunts?
Those clamoring unbelievers,
All who remain,
Will they not conquer them and return?”
The leopard grew angry
And unleashed terrible wrath.
It was not the Kytay enemy,
But Baltay, who was speaking,
Whom he nearly swallowed up.
When Akbaltay heard this,
Strength drained from his forearms,
The covering fell from his heart.
What could poor Baltay do?
Having spoken those words,
His eyes began to dart,
His feet began to dangle.
The leopard of terrible wrath
Rumbled and burned with anger.
Watching him, Akbaltay
Despaired of his entrusted life.
'Mighty Allah, almighty power,
May you keep Manas safe,' he prayed.
The gray-maned hero spoke in fury:
“Ever since I became Manas,
Against those damned Kytay
How often have I unleashed wrath!
On this dark day, elder, think:
Before this, of the Kytay,
How many have I slaughtered!
Elder Baltay, what are you saying?
Since sitting astride a horse,
Since charging the enemy with a roar,
Against the black Kytay and Manchus,
Before I reached twelve,
How much trouble did I cause!
When the Kytay imposed their rule,
When they committed extreme oppression,
When they sought a fight,
I was first to wreak havoc;
I seized their Kalmyk.
Having seized him then,
I cut his throat.
Where, then, is my death?
Only yesterday, Baltay, you were there:
I raised a quarrel over the ordo game;
I seized their gold outright.
